'''Firefox Lockwise''' (formerly '''Lockbox'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Firefox schirmt Nutzer stärker vor Werbe-Trackern ab |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000104345818/firefox-schirmt-nutzer-staerker-vor-werbe-trackern-ab |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=DER STANDARD |language=de-AT}}</ref>) is a deprecated<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/mozilla-ends-support-for-firefox-lockwise-password-management-app-strands-ios-users/|title=Mozilla ends support for Firefox Lockwise password management app, strands iOS users|website=[[ZDNet]]}}</ref> [[password manager]] for the [[Firefox]] web browser, as well as the mobile operating systems [[iOS]] and [[Android (operating system)|Android]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Lance|last1=Whitney|date=August 21, 2019|access-date=2019-11-18|title=How to Manage Web Passwords With Firefox Lockwise|url=https://www.pcmag.com/feature/367772/how-to-manage-web-passwords-with-firefox-lockwise|website=PCMAG}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Catherine|last=Ellis|date=2019-06-04|access-date=2019-11-18|title=Mozilla launches new desktop password manager, Firefox Lockwise|url=https://www.techradar.com/uk/news/mozilla-launches-new-desktop-password-manager-firefox-lockwise|website=TechRadar}}</ref> On desktop, Lockwise was simply part of Firefox,<ref name="FF70" /> whereas on iOS and Android it was available as a standalone app. If [[Firefox Sync]] was activated (with a Firefox account), then Lockwise synced passwords between Firefox installations across devices.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Es muss nicht immer Chrome sein: Die besten Alternativen zu Googles Browser |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000113659784/es-muss-nicht-immer-chrome-sein-die-besten-alternativen-zu |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=DER STANDARD |language=de-AT}}</ref> It also featured a built-in [[random password generator]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-06 |title=Firefox Lockwise: Tutorial zu dem Firefox-Passwort-Manager |url=https://www.computerbild.de/artikel/cb-Tipps-Software-Firefox-Lockwise-Tutorial-zu-dem-Firefox-Passwort-Manager-38432151.html |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=COMPUTER BILD |language=de}}</ref> The application and branding have since been "phased out."<ref name="GitHub">{{cite web|quote=The lockwise app is being phased out.|url=https://github.com/mozilla/bedrock/issues/10166|title=Replace Lockwise with VPN on various pages · Issue #10166 · mozilla/bedrock|last=Brown|first=Dan|date=April 22, 2021|website=GitHub}}</ref>

== History ==

Developed by [[Mozilla Corporation|Mozilla]], it was originally named Firefox '''Lockbox''' in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2019-11-18|title=Firefox Lockwise Aims to Revamp Browser Password Management|url=https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/firefox-lockwise-aims-to-revamp-browser-password-management/|website=BleepingComputer}}</ref> It was renamed "Lockwise" in May 2019.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2019-11-18|title=New Privacy Features for Mozilla Firefox, Lockwise Is Live|url=https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-privacy-features-for-mozilla-firefox-lockwise-is-live/|website=BleepingComputer}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Rename "Firefox Lockbox" to "Firefox Lockwise" after May 28 |url= https://github.com/mozilla/bedrock/issues/7242 |website=GitHub |quote=Lockbox is getting a new name on 28 May [for the "Trailhead" release, a product update.] | date= 25 May 2019}}</ref> It was introduced for iOS on 10 July 2018 as part of the Test Pilot program.<ref name=Lockbox>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.mozilla.org/blog/2018/07/10/introducing-firefoxs-first-mobile-test-pilot-experiments-lockbox-and-notes|title=Introducing Firefox's First Mobile Test Pilot Experiments: Lockbox and Notes|last=Nguyen|first=Nick|website=The Mozilla Blog|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-26}}</ref> 
On 26 March 2019, it was released for Android.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.mozilla.org/blog/2019/03/26/firefox-lockbox-now-on-android-keeping-your-passwords-safe|title=Firefox Lockbox Now on Android, Keeping your Passwords Safe|last=Nguyen|first=Nick|website=The Mozilla Blog|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-26}}</ref>

On desktop, Lockwise started out as a browser addon. [[Alpha release|Alpha]]s were released between March and August 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Firefox Lockbox for Desktop |url=https://github.com/mozilla-lockwise/lockwise-addon/releases |publisher=Firefox |date=10 Aug 2019 }} (Firefox addon repository)</ref> Since Firefox version 70, Lockwise has been integrated into the browser<ref>{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Speed |date=22 October 2019|access-date=2019-11-18|title=Minigame: Celebrate Firefox 70's release by finding a website with 70+ trackers blocked|url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2019/10/22/firefox_70/|website=www.theregister.co.uk}}</ref> (accessible at {{code|about:logins}}),<ref name="FF70">{{cite web |title=Firefox 70.0 release notes |url=https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/70.0/releasenotes/ |website=Mozilla |date=October 22, 2019}}</ref> having replaced a basic password manager presented in a popup window.<ref>{{cite web |title=Password Manager in Firefox |url=https://support.mozilla.org/kb/password-manager-remember-delete-edit-logins?redirectlocale=en-US&redirectslug=password-manager-remember-delete-change-and-import |website=Firefox Help |access-date=26 October 2019 |quote=Password Manager is now Firefox Lockwise! The interface for managing usernames and passwords was entirely redesigned and is now based on the Firefox Lockwise add-on.}}</ref>

Mozilla ended support for Firefox Lockwise on December 13, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2021/11/23/22798811/mozilla-is-ending-support-for-firefox-lockwise-password-manager|title=Mozilla is ending support for its Firefox password manager sync app|first=Umar|last=Shakir|date=November 23, 2021|website=[[The Verge]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/mozilla-is-shutting-down-its-password-management-app|title=Mozilla Is Shutting Down Its Password Management App|website=[[PCMag]]|date=22 November 2021 }}</ref>

As of January 2026, Lockwise is still fully functional on Android to this day.
